title: What Photonic Computing Architecture Is
provenance: Public research knowledge: documented developments, published research, and established technical references. Real, fact-checked records.
description: Photonic computing architectures compute with light instead of electrons: matrix multiplications happen as light passes through meshes of interferometers, at the speed of light and with minimal heat. A photonic processor encodes data in light intensity or phase, performs the linear algebra optically, and converts back to electronics only at the boundaries. This record is the entry point of the teaching ladder for Photonic Computing Architecture: start here, then move through the research state, the specifications, the public developments, the open challenges, and finally each piece needed to build it.
key_points: Photonic Computing Architecture in one line: Photonic computing architectures compute with light instead of electrons: matrix multiplications happen as light passes through meshes of interferometers, at the speed of light and with minimal heat.
Why it matters: Optical matrix multiplication is nearly free in energy and latency — the two walls choking AI hardware scaling..
Where it is used: AI inference acceleration, optical neural networks, signal processing, and data-center interconnect compute..
Ladder rank 1 — the foundation. Everything else builds on this.

t: Current Research State of Photonic Computing Architecture
title: Current Research State of Photonic Computing Architecture
provenance: Public research knowledge: documented developments, published research, and established technical references. Real, fact-checked records.
description: Startups and labs have demonstrated photonic tensor cores doing neural-network inference with competitive accuracy, microring and Mach-Zehnder meshes scaling to hundreds of modes, and co-packaged optics for data centers. Research targets larger meshes, on-chip nonlinearity for all-optical networks, and training. The gap: size (photonic components are microns, not nanometers) and the electro-optic conversion overhead. Research moves in three waves: laboratory proof of concept, scaled prototypes under controlled conditions, and field trials. Photonic Computing Architecture currently sits at the stage described above, and the pieces records show what each wave still needs.

t: Challenges and Open Problems in Photonic Computing Architecture
title: Challenges and Open Problems in Photonic Computing Architecture
provenance: Public research knowledge: documented developments, published research, and established technical references. Real, fact-checked records.
description: Photonics does not shrink like transistors: a useful mesh is millimeters across. Analog precision limits model accuracy, lasers and thermal drift need control, and every conversion between light and electricity costs energy. Training on photonic hardware is still early. Every challenge here is a design requirement in disguise: solve it and the technology moves forward. The pieces records each carry the challenge they exist to answer.
